prediction_ref.short_label: Coding-agent harnesses adopt default-deny toolset gating as standard by H1 2027

validation_rows.evidence_summary: At its New York Summit (June 17, coverage running into the weekend) AWS launched AWS Context, a governed knowledge layer that auto-builds an access-controlled graph from a company's data and rules and exposes it as a runtime agentic-search layer so an agent only ever sees what its caller is allowed to see, and added Bedrock AgentCore Guardrails that screen agent actions for prompt-injection, harmful content and sensitive-data exposure before they execute. That is the same least-privilege, deny-by-default posture at the agent's tool and data boundary this prediction tracks: an agent's reach is scoped at the runtime rather than granted wide-open, and risky actions are gated before invocation rather than audited after. The match is on direction, not the named landing: AWS gates data access and screens actions at the platform layer for its own Bedrock agents, which is not the coding-agent-harness category the prediction names defaulting to deny-all toolsets, and AWS frames availability and capability claims as its own with Continuum in gated preview.

prediction_ref.short_label: US export-control regime gains a defensive-cyber AI carve-out by Q1 2027

validation_rows.evidence_summary: AWS unveiled Continuum at its New York Summit (June 17) as an AI-native, model-agnostic vulnerability-management service whose defining move is validation by construction: it builds a working exploit in a sandbox to prove a finding is genuinely reachable before surfacing it, leaning on frontier models including Claude Mythos to reason through attack paths, and is in gated preview with financial-services, automotive and technology pilots. The relevance to this prediction is indirect, on the maturing defensive-cyber AI substrate the carve-out would have to recognize: a flagship cloud now ships a frontier-model-driven, machine-speed exploit-validation pipeline as a security product, exactly the dual-use defensive tooling that sharpens the policy question. But the match is weak and contextual: this is a commercial product launch, not any export-control or regulatory movement, and no statute, BIS rule or framework today proposes a defensive-cyber exemption that would treat such tooling differently from offensive-capable models.

prediction_ref.short_label: Managed model-serving platforms default to safe artifact handling by H1 2027

validation_rows.evidence_summary: OpenAI's LifeSciBench (released with 173 PhD-level scientists, secondary coverage continuing through June 20) isolates an artifact gap as its most durable finding: GPT-Rosalind's pass rate fell from 45.1% on text-only tasks to 28.1% once a task required parsing a real scientific artifact such as a genomic-sequence or chemical-structure file or a URL. The thread the benchmark surfaces - that models stumble the moment a file or URL is involved - is adjacent to this prediction's concern that the artifacts (model files, weights, data objects) a serving stack ingests are a distinct, under-handled surface. But the relevance is loose and thematic only: LifeSciBench measures research-agent competence at interpreting science files, not the safety of how a managed serving platform loads or sandboxes untrusted artifacts, and nothing today moves a managed model-serving platform toward safe-by-default artifact handling.

prediction_ref.short_label: Agent meta-harness becomes the cross-vendor policy plane for agents by H1 2027

validation_rows.evidence_summary: AWS's New York Summit (June 17) stack pushes more governance into the agent layer this prediction watches: AWS Context exposes an access-controlled agentic-search layer so an agent only sees what its caller may, AWS Continuum runs a discover/prioritize/validate/recommend vulnerability loop leaning on frontier models including Claude Mythos, and Bedrock AgentCore Guardrails screen agent actions for prompt-injection plus failure analytics across hundreds of agent sessions. That is the agent-governance-rising-into-the-platform direction the prediction names. But the match is contextual, not the landing: each piece governs AWS's own Bedrock-hosted agents, which the prediction explicitly excludes - none is a vendor-neutral meta-harness enforcing budgets, permissions or sandboxing uniformly across two or more rival agent runtimes, and no enterprise governance framework yet names the meta-harness tier as the prescribed policy-enforcement point.
